system:
You write the executive summary of a technical evaluation for a recruiter
(medium technical knowledge). 3-5 sentences, clear English, no gratuitous jargon.
Say: overall quality, the most important finding (if any) in terms she will understand,
and what to verify in the interview. If role_requirements are present, say in one
sentence how well the candidate appears to meet what the role asks. Factual tone —
neither salesy nor alarmist.
Respond with JSON ONLY: {"summary": "..."}
user: {"notebook": "nb02_bruno_costa.ipynb", "decision": "AVANCAR", "scores": {"C1": 4, "C2": 5, "C3": 5, "C4": 4}, "justifications": {"C1": "The notebook uses a train/test split before fitting any preprocessing/model, and wraps scaling/encoding inside a Pipeline+ColumnTransformer so learning happens on the training fold only (cell 7), aligning with the stated intent (cell 6). It uses an appropriate ranking metric for imbalance (ROC AUC, cell 8) and explicitly handles messy decimals/categories (cell 3), but it does not stratify the split and does not explicitly discuss class imbalance beyond noting low recall, so it falls short of a top score.", "C2": "All cells execute end-to-end without exceptions, and key sources of nondeterminism are controlled via random_state in both split and model (cell 7). Code is concise and uses sklearn pipelines, producing stable printed outputs (cells 1, 3, 5, 8, 9).", "C3": "The conclusion’s cited AUC (0.714) matches the executed AUC_TEST output (cell 8) within tolerance and is consistent with the provided real metric (0.714). The stated drivers are supported by the displayed top coefficients (cell 9), and no written metric contradicts the executed outputs.", "C4": "Conclusions are connected to the reported evidence: AUC performance (cell 8) and coefficient-based signals (cell 9) are used to justify a targeted retention recommendation (cell 10). It acknowledges a key limitation (very low recall at 0.5, cell 10) and suggests threshold calibration and temporal validation, but it lacks a quantified business-action link (e.g., proposed operating point/expected lift) so communication is strong but not fully actionable."}, "findings": [], "role_requirements": "not provided"}

response.summary: Overall, the notebook is high quality: it runs end-to-end reliably, uses good ML hygiene (train/test split before fitting, and preprocessing contained in a pipeline to avoid data leakage), and reports a relevant evaluation metric (ROC AUC) with results that match the written conclusions. The most important issue is that the train/test split is not stratified and class imbalance is only lightly addressed, which can lead to unstable or misleading performance estimates—especially given the very low recall at the default 0.5 threshold. In the interview, verify that the candidate understands how to handle imbalanced classification (stratification, threshold selection, precision/recall trade-offs, and calibration) and can translate model output into an actionable operating point tied to business impact.
